note: Cases chosen from the REAL NASA data (2005–2025): both places in every pair have a significant Mann-Kendall trend (Hamed-Rao + Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, q < 0.05) in opposite directions on the case layer. Numbers in the summaries are Sen-slope changes over 2005–2025. 'expected' is only used by the mock generator. 'tour' marks the guided-example case. Re-check with scripts if the data is regenerated.

cases.title: Southern Amazon vs. Lake Chad
cases.summary: The southern Amazon (Rondônia) gets much less rain than in 2005 (about −58%), while the Lake Chad basin in the Sahel is getting wetter (about +19%).

cases.title: Punjab vs. Lake Victoria
cases.summary: Groundwater pumping for farming drains northern India (about −79 cm of water since 2005), while Africa's largest lake region gains water (about +111 cm).

cases.title: California vs. Murray-Darling
cases.summary: Two big farming regions: California's Central Valley keeps losing water (about −32 cm), while Australia's Murray-Darling Basin recovers after its millennium drought (about +13 cm).

cases.title: Tehran vs. the Sudd
cases.summary: Iran's aquifers are being emptied (about −59 cm since 2005), while the Nile's great wetland in South Sudan stores more water (about +24 cm).

cases.title: Beijing vs. Odesa
cases.summary: Northern China gets more rain than in 2005 (about +48%), while southern Ukraine dries out (about −18%) and loses water reserves.

cases.title: Khartoum vs. Seville
cases.summary: A rare place that cooled: Khartoum is about 1.1 °C cooler as the Sahel got wetter, while southern Spain warmed about 1.7 °C since 2005.
